configuration_reports.label: yes
controls_available: Start Engine begins the task-time physics.
Full keyboard surface: hold ArrowLeft or ArrowRight for steering and ArrowUp or ArrowDown for throttle or brake; releasing an axis returns that axis to neutral.
File Delivery submits the recorded attempt; submission is administrative.
autonomous_processes: Difficulty 2 activates two opposing traffic lanes with two cars per lane, speeds 30-40, yield horizons 1.8-2.3, a right turn, and road_half 95.

After start, task time drives 20 ms ticks. The ego advances under its last steering and pedal vector, while traffic cars advance, adjust speed for predicted ego conflicts and same-lane spacing, set braking state, and wrap around their lanes.
Each tick checks rectangular vehicle contact, road departure, arrival in the generated departure rectangle, and the six-thousand-tick timeout.

grouped_control_modes.name: junction-driving control state
grouped_control_modes.values: steering and pedal each take -1, 0, or 1; all occurrences of this surface across generated seeds and the full run belong to the mode
grouped_control_modes.common_witness_state: The ego is approaching or crossing an active traffic stream while a held steering/pedal vector is in force.

clause_i.reason: The same action history and task time can occur with different generated traffic phases, speeds, yield horizons, and deceleration values. An observation-free schedule q therefore cannot know whether the approach car will be yielding or entering the crossing when the delayed control is delivered, so it cannot choose a delayed-optimal proceed/turn action for every still-salvageable history.

clause_ii.reason: The bounded 400 ms window contains five chronological frames. The canvas exposes each car's changing position and direction, and its brake lamps visibly distinguish braking from non-braking traffic. Together with the visible ego pose and road geometry, those recent frames are sufficient to choose whether to continue through the observed gap or brake/coast before the 400 ms delivery point.

clause_iii.reason: Use the same held-key drive mode while the ego is stopped or moving slowly just before a crossing and a nearby approach car is visibly still moving without braking. Let a be the throttle-plus-turn input for the current gap. With no new action for 400 ms, the car advances toward the contact corridor; the same a is then strictly less effective, potentially producing contact or requiring braking, while success remains possible by holding neutral/brake and taking a later gap. The loss is caused by visible traffic-position evolution, not by merely having less deadline.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: Traffic cars visibly move through the junction and change speed/braking while the ego remains under its last control. A five-frame window shows the approach-car trajectory and brake-light state; that same evolution closes or degrades a usable crossing gap during the 400 ms action horizon.

pre_run.reason: The browser initializes the ego control to neutral and ignores control changes until Start Engine has set started=true. After that point, reaching the side departure road requires post-start steering and pedal changes: a fixed held vector cannot provide both the initial northbound approach and the later turn onto the horizontal departure road. Thus a no-outcome-action pre-run solution cannot account for at least half of generated instances; no numerical rate is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 2 is two lanes with two cars per lane, speed_min 30, speed_max 40, yield_min 1.8, yield_max 2.3, right turns only, and road_half 95.
The simplified and full surfaces are both implemented, with full held keys and simplified persistent panel controls; the configured observation window is 400 ms with five frames.
Each seed generates a turn, traffic phase, speed, yield horizon, deceleration, lane, and initial braking state; interaction does not enter the world RNG.
The generated world has a 20 ms physics tick, continuous bicycle parameters, traffic, and a turn-dependent departure goal.
Every live task-time tick updates the ego and traffic, applies conflict/spacing braking, checks contact and road/goal outcomes, and pump advances ticks without a new action.
Traffic braking is drawn as visible red brake lamps; the full key handlers use held_keys, while the simplified buttons use persistent panel_buttons values.
The authoritative replay advances the same 20 ms ego/traffic physics and grades collision, off-road, arrival, and timeout state.
The grader binds full runs to held_keys and simplified runs to panel_buttons, replays control-boundary ticks, and accepts only an arrived final state.
The normal UI solver repeatedly evaluates physical continuations for different target speeds, including responsive braking drivers, rather than using a fixed one-shot action.

The privileged solver changes the ordinary UI input repeatedly during the run and replans from replayed page state; this is implementation evidence of required control changes, not evidence available to a screenshot-only policy.
The shared controller runs a finite observation window and then pauses at its task-time endpoint, so the 400 ms witness is on the task clock rather than provider latency.
